topics.title: Matrix Transformations
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Identify transformation matrices for reflection, rotation and enlargement. (k, u, s)
Determine the image given the object and transformation matrix, on a coordinate grid. (u, s)
Identify the matrix of transformation when the object and its image are given. (u, s)
Determine the inverse of a transformation matrix. (u)
Use the inverse matrix to find the object when the image is given. (u, s)
Identify the relationship between area scale factor and determinant of the transformation matrix. (u)
Determines a single matrix for successive transformations. (u, v/a)

body.text: A 2x2 matrix can represent a geometric transformation: multiplying it by a point's column vector (x, y) gives the transformed point. A 90° anti-clockwise rotation about the origin has matrix [[0,-1],[1,0]]; a reflection in the line y=x has matrix [[0,1],[1,0]].
Apply the rotation matrix [[0,-1],[1,0]] to the point (3, 2): new x = 0(3)+(-1)(2) = -2, new y = 1(3)+0(2) = 3. So (3,2) maps to (-2,3), matching the 90° anti-clockwise rule (x,y)->(-y,x).

The determinant of a transformation matrix equals its area scale factor: a matrix with determinant 4 makes any shape's area 4 times larger. A negative determinant means the transformation also flips (reverses) the shape's orientation. To reverse a transformation, apply the inverse matrix to the image to recover the original object — for a transformation matrix M, applying M⁻¹ undoes it.

Two transformations applied one after another (first A, then B) combine into a single matrix BA (multiply in that order — B on the left, since it acts last). This single combined matrix maps the original object straight to the final image in one step.
